head: 5c7b7172da449a43835887b059dad52fe150ce84
summary: NORM-1 normalization class decision, recorded for later synchronization with the bitty-terminal-docs security corpus. This is a CarryCtx handoff record only: no docs repository was edited. NORMATIVE DECISION: the redaction normalization class in bitty-devtools is every code point above U+007F that Unicode classifies as Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, or as general category Cf (Other Format), or as White_Space. Membership is decided by Unicode character properties only; no hand-written range list is normative in either language. Membership is 4225 code points in 29 ranges for Unicode 17.0. RATIONALE AND EVIDENCE: every member renders as nothing at all, as a format control or a default-ignorable code point, or as blank, as a non-ASCII space separator, so a hostile producer can inject any member to break a literal credential pattern match without changing what the operator sees on screen. Cf is included alongside Default_Ignorable_Code_Point because the two are not the same set: 32 non-ASCII Cf code points are not Default_Ignorable in Unicode 17.0, namely U+0600 to U+0605, U+06DD, U+070F, U+0890 to U+0891, U+08E2, U+FFF9 to U+FFFB, U+110BD, U+110CD and U+13430 to U+1343F, and all of them are invisible format controls, so omitting Cf would leave a bypass hole. The prior hand-written Rust table covered Default_Ignorable plus non-ASCII White_Space and additionally FFF9 to FFFB, 4196 code points; measured against the prior TypeScript property predicate plus its legacy list the two sets were identical, so the reported U+2065 and U+FFF0 to U+FFF8 divergence was not reproducible, and the real defect was that the class was defined twice with no gate, which would surface as silent drift at the next engine Unicode bump. CONTROLS ESCAPED, NOT NORMALIZED: C0, DEL and C1 controls are outside the class on purpose. They are escaped for rendering and never silently deleted, so an escape is never swallowed. U+0085 is the single code point in both sets, Cc and White_Space; it is removed for matching and escaped for rendering, and both implementations order the branches identically. IMPLEMENTATION AND GATE: src/redaction.ts owns the TypeScript predicate isNormalizationSeparator over the three Unicode properties; crates/devtools-client/src/redaction.rs owns NORM_1_RANGES, a 29-entry generated table from the same definition, never hand-curated. tests/fixtures/redaction-normalization-class.txt pins all 4225 members and 266 near-miss non-members, including every ASCII code point and both neighbours of every class range, and both the TypeScript and the Rust test suites execute it, so any future membership change on either side fails a gate in both languages. A second TypeScript test re-derives the class from the three properties and compares it to the pin, so a pinned row that stops following from the definition is also caught. RELATED NORMATIVE DECISION from the same round: a bare credential-bearing configuration name is sensitive when the name segment is SCREAMING, that is SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, CREDENTIAL or API_KEY, but not when it is lower or mixed case, because the case-insensitive variant made ordinary prose a finding and would have destroyed report usefulness. SUGGESTED CORPUS SYNC: bitty-terminal-docs security should state NORM-1 as a property-defined class, state that C0, DEL and C1 are escaped rather than normalized, state that a bare SCREAMING credential name is sensitive while prose mentioning a key name is not, and state that redaction must never be weaker in one client implementation than in another, with the differential-probe direction requirement that Rust never redacts strictly less than TypeScript.
